question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's set $u=\log{\left(\frac{x}{5} \right)}.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,1\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $5$ | $5 e$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $1$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{25}\int_{5}^{5 e}\frac{3\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}}{\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{6}{25}\int_{5}^{5 e}\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}\cdot \frac{1}{\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{6}{5}\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{6}{5}\int_{0}^{1}{u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(3\cdot \frac{{u}^{3/2}}{3/2}\right)|_{0}^{1} \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(2\cdot {u}^{3/2}\right)|_{0}^{1} \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(2({1}^{3/2}-{0}^{3/2})\right) \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(2(1-0)\right) \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(2\right)\end{aligned}
$$
